Your AI vendor lock-in problem may have just gotten a solution — from an unexpected source.

Google introduced the Gemini agent at its Gemini at Work event this week. It is a persistent enterprise agent that operates across work surfaces and can select among multiple underlying models. The critical part: enterprise context and workflows remain stable while the model underneath changes.

Until now, choosing an enterprise AI platform meant coupling your workflows, data pipelines, and institutional knowledge to a single model. Switching costs were high by design. Google deliberately broke that pattern.

Atlassian reinforced the same idea the same week. AMP, launched at Team '26 Europe, gives AI agents their own identity, scoped authority, and visible participation inside team workflows. The message from two major platforms simultaneously: the agent layer is becoming the durable enterprise asset. The model is becoming interchangeable compute.

This splits enterprise AI procurement into two distinct strategic decisions — agent infrastructure and model selection. CTOs who recognize this shift early and architect accordingly will maintain optionality as foundation models continue to leapfrog each other quarter over quarter. Those who keep bundling agent logic and model choice will accumulate technical debt that compounds with every new release cycle.
